If A denotes ‘+’, B denotes ‘×’, C denotes ‘−’, and D denotes ‘÷’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation?

94 A 16 B 3 C 86 A 14 D 7 = ?
questions.solution:
Explanation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2042326d26ec7b593e52bbbdd22d890b59b1e59f92be81a7235509e9af1c4625.png] 

Decoding the information, 

 
 

 
 
Letter

 
 
 
A

 
 
 
B

 
 
 
C

 
 
 
D

 
 
 

 
 
Means

 
 
 
+

 
 
 
×

 
 
 
-

 
 
 
÷

 
 
 

Given:

94 A 16 B 3 C 86 A 14 D 7 = ?

After replacing the signs from left to right and using the BODMAS rule,

= 94 + 16 × 3 - 86 + __**14 ÷ 7**__

= 94 + __**16 × 3**__ - 86 + 2

= 94 + 48 - 86 + 2

= 58

Hence, “58” is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Two Statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All queens are kings.

Some kings are aces.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some kings are queens.

II. All queens are aces.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
Explanation:

The least possible Venn Diagram is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ed1a0a4baaae21db905ddfe1200f25e2e4b1a347ebd3ce47bbcd039ef7d8d642.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some kings are queens. → Follows (because all queens are kings, so we can say that some kings are definitely queens.)

II. All queens are aces. → Does not follow (because some kings are aces and all queens are kings, hence we cannot definitely say that all queens are definitely aces.) 

Hence, “Only conclusion I follows.”.

questions.question:
Arrange the following farming processes in a logical and meaningful order.

1. Winnowing

2. Sowing

3. Threshing

4. Harvesting

5. Ploughing
questions.solution:
**Explanation:**

 
• **Ploughing**: First of all farmer plough the fields. first of all, the soil is prepared for growing crop by the farmer. By ploughing, he loosens and turns the soil, which helps roots of the crop to penetrate deeper into the soil and respire easily
 
• **Sowing of seeds**: After preparing the soil, the farmer selects the best quality of seeds to ensure a healthy crop and maximum grain production and sows the seeds of the crop.
 
• **Harvesting: **After the ripening of the crop, the farmer cuts it, it is called harvesting.
 
• **Threshing:** After harvesting, the crop is dried to remove any moisture. Then its grains are separated out from the chaff
